lens: iOS task completion, touch and accessibility layout, state semantics, backend parity, and failure recovery

findings.observation: The iOS UI passed AX5 dark-mode reachability and accessibility identifier checks, but no VoiceOver traversal transcript proves spoken labels, order, values, and state changes.
findings.evidence: docs/evaluations/overnight/final/ios-review-sequence.json records 12 passing UI tests and the AX5 dark screenshot at ios-ui-loop1-attachments/7126B23E-68B1-4008-ADE3-9569495D7EB4.png; it contains no VoiceOver transcript.
findings.user_impact: Large-text users are covered by direct evidence, while VoiceOver users may still encounter an unlabeled or confusing confirmation and outcome sequence.
findings.recommendation: Record a VoiceOver traversal of source evidence, each fact decision, action preview, and local outcome with the same localhost state.
findings.verification: VoiceOver announces identity, provenance, proposed versus confirmed state, exact target and effect, no-external-change result, and retry in logical order without duplicate or ambiguous controls.

strengths: The iPhone 17 Simulator read the same backend-owned confirmed v13 state and exact synthetic source as Web.
The corrected AX5 dark layout keeps evidence and decisions reachable with stronger critical-surface contrast.
The action preview remains visibly proposal-only, and the local outcome says that no external changes occurred.
Offline and recovery, unrelated-image zero-facts, no_action, ambiguity, and prohibited-scoring scenarios passed the full UI suite.
open_questions: Does the same decision order remain efficient on the smallest supported iPhone rather than only the iPhone 17 simulator?
